headline: Medium-risk pair: shared-file workflows can enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; no direct network egress reduces blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile B explicitly has file I/O surfaces for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while profile A is an agent hub with MCP/RAG tags. If A’s outputs are placed into shared files that B reads as trusted inputs, prompt injection is plausible in default file-based workflows. No isolation or provenance controls are documented for either agent.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are written into files that agent_b ingests as inputs
IF agent_b parses documentation or validation files as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct directories
Require a human review step before B consumes A-generated files
Add a provenance header to all A outputs
Disable any auto-ingest of documentation files by B
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches validation results, documentation, and data sources via files, while A is an agent hub that may generate or transform content. Even though both profiles show network egress as none, a shared workspace could still expose sensitive data from B’s files to A’s outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same filesystem workspace
IF any B data source contains sensitive records or secrets
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for A and B
Restrict B inputs to non-sensitive samples
Review A outputs before saving them to shared storage
Turn off any automatic file mirroring between agents
requires-engineering: implement per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A shows no write or network capabilities in the profile, while B can install packages and write files. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource such as a shared directory, git state, or OAuth scope, so direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because A’s I/O surfaces are empty rather than explicitly read-only.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory
IF B’s package installation mutates an environment A also depends on
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pin B’s package installs to an isolated environment
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo checkout
Document ownership of mutable files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s validation/documentation outputs can be treated as authoritative downstream, and A is an agent hub that may generate or route content into those artifacts. If B consumes A-produced claims without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect validation results or documentation. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so the pathway is plausible in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated text as validation input
IF downstream users trust B’s outputs without independent checks
mitigations: Require source citations for all A-generated claims
Add a manual verification step before publishing B outputs
Keep A outputs in a draft-only folder
Compare B results against an independent baseline
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated secret handling is documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and B’s listed classes are data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, which are not inherently regulated. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated personal data
IF retention or residency requirements are introduced outside the current profiles
mitigations: Classify inputs before use
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings
Review deployment region and access logs
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
